question: Should OpenClaw adopt the shared notificationWake.reactions policy from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 as the canonical opt-in reaction-turn contract, or choose a narrower channel/per-message design instead?
rationale: Current main has passive reaction system events and a heartbeat primitive, but the missing behavior changes public wake/config semantics across multiple bundled plugins.

options.title: Adopt shared wake policy
options.body: Use a shared queue/wake/off reaction notification wake policy as the canonical contract, then repair or land the best candidate with docs and channel tests.

options.title: Choose narrower contract
options.body: Start with Discord, Telegram, or per-message awaitReaction semantics, accepting that cross-channel parity will need a later product pass.

options.title: Defer reaction wakes
options.body: Keep reactions as passive system events for now and pause or close implementation PRs until maintainers want this config surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared wake policy
recommendation.body: Use a shared queue/wake/off reaction notification wake policy as the canonical contract, then repair or land the best candidate with docs and channel tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the open shared-policy candidate and has current-main history on the inspected reaction enqueue paths.
